thread:
claire: Quick idea — instead of per-chunk strong checksums in a manifest, what about a lightweight probabilistic verification layer (rolling/checkpointed sampling) to detect corrupted transfers early and only verify suspicious chunks fully?
dan: Interesting. So runtime samples a few bytes per chunk, or computes a tiny rolling checksum window, and if mismatch -> full checksum lookup/repair? That could reduce manifest size and verify cost.
mei: Danger: false negatives. We must bound probability of undetected corruption. For storage-level bit flips it's probably ok, but adversarial corruption or gzip misalignments could sneak by.
claire: Right — assume non-adversarial. We can pick sampling rate/positions based on RNG seeded by shard-id so all replicas sample same offsets. Add a manifest field with a small 64-bit Bloom-ish summary per-shard and a seed. If sample matches summary -> accept; if not -> fetch full checksums or reget range.
dan: That keeps manifest tiny. Also helpful for compressed shards: we can record sample offsets after compression mapping. But we still need an explicit path for strict models: always verify full checksums.
mei: Ops notes: add metrics: sample_mismatch_count, fallback_full_verify_count, undetected_estimate (probabilistic). Also config knobs: sample_rate, strict_models list.
claire: Implementation stub: loader does range-gets for streaming. For each chunk it computes sample_hash = rolling64(chosen_offsets). Compare to manifest.summary[chunk_index] (if present). If mismatch -> schedule a full-range reget and mark chunk REPAIR_PENDING.
build-bot: Canary scheduled: loader-probe with sampling verification will be rolled to us-west-2 on 2026-04-03T02:00Z per infra calendar.
dan: Tests: synthetic corruption harness that flips random bytes and measures false negative rate for different sample_rate. Also end-to-end perf test for p99 impact. I can take that.
mei: If we add this, we must document compatibility: existing safetensors bundles without summary manifest -> fallback to full-checksum behavior.
claire: OK I'll draft a tiny manifest prototype (shard.summary.v1) and a short risk note. Landing plan: opt-in via config flag sampling_verify=true for canary, default off.
dan: sounds good. :+1:
